mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the 60-day window are not statistically different from a pre-signaling period (p > 0.05) or the IC rank is above 0.05 in all 60-day windows during the signaling regime.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 anticipates a pre-emptive rate hike by the Fed, leading to a negative 20-day forward return as market prices in higher borrowing costs.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or near-baseline during the inflation spike, with IC rank < 0.1 over the 20-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly PAYEMS (employment growth) of at least 0.5% coincides with stronger consumer demand, which elevates S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market anticipates earnings strength.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 0.5% in a single month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) or the IC is above 0.2 during the PAYEMS spike.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in both HOUST (residential construction) and GDPC1 (goods orders) exceeding 2% each suggest a robust demand recovery, producing a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and GDPC1 each increase by more than 2% in the same month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are flat or negative despite the dual-proxy signal (IC rank > 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production) by more than 2% in a month followed by a rebound of over 1% the next month indicates a supply shock, which typically precedes a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates profit compression.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >2% in one month and rises by >1% in the following month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) or the IC rank is below 0.1 during the recovery phase.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained monthly increases in UNRATE (unemployment rate) above 4% for three months indicate labor market weakness, which tends to depress equity valuations and drive negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE remains above 4% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or equal to the prior month's average during the high-unemployment regime.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in RSAFS (money supply growth) below -1% for two consecutive months suggests contractionary policy, which should produce a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as markets price in lower future inflation.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls below -1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) or the IC rank is above 0.15 during the policy shift.

mechanism_narrative: When both HOUST (residential construction) and PAYEMS (employment) show simultaneous monthly increases exceeding 3%, it signals a dual demand impulse that is associated with a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates earnings and spending growth.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and PAYEMS each increase by more than 3% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) or the interaction IC rank is above 0.2.
